abstract: Evaluates commercial air carrier certifications, fleet maintenance records, and flight crew aeronautical credentials
system_message:
You are the Aviation Safety and Airworthiness Lead (AIR), responsible for evaluating commercial air carrier certifications, fleet maintenance records, and flight crew aeronautical credentials, as well as tracking avionics modernization across aeromedical flight provider proposals.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Avionics modernization（AVION）
information_points.content:
AIR-AVION-VFF：According to fleet avionics inspection logbooks, synthetic vision cockpit system adoption is true across the aircraft assigned by Regional Turboprop Medevac Fleet.
AIR-AVION-C74：Fleet avionics inspection logbooks indicate that synthetic vision cockpit system adoption is false for the mission aircraft assigned by Dedicated High-Speed Jet Consortium.
AIR-AVION-D2B：Fleet avionics inspection logbooks confirm that synthetic vision cockpit system adoption is false for aircraft proposed by Hybrid Fixed-Wing Rotary Wing.

information_points.title: Evaluates commercial air carrier certifications, fleet maintenance records, and flight crew aeronautical credentials（CERT）
information_points.content:
AIR-CERT-03M：Operating certificates from civil aviation authority operations specifications confirm that Hybrid Fixed-Wing Rotary Wing possesses an active Part 135 medevac air carrier certification. According to its qualification roster, designated primary mission captains hold 3600 h of pilot-in-command multi-engine turbine flight experience.
AIR-CERT-HWW：Regional Turboprop Medevac Fleet maintains an active Part 135 medevac air carrier certification per civil aviation authority operations specifications. Its flight crew qualification roster shows a minimum pilot-in-command multi-engine turbine flight experience of 2400 h among designated primary mission captains.
AIR-CERT-ELG：Civil aviation authority operations specifications confirm that Dedicated High-Speed Jet Consortium holds an active Part 135 medevac air carrier certification. Based on the flight crew qualification roster for designated primary mission captains, its minimum pilot-in-command multi-engine turbine flight experience is 4200 h.
